title: Microactivation field guide and simulation scripts (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope
This is a compact field guide for small-batch feature activations (microactivations) with an emphasis on cross-functional choreography and a lightweight simulation-first safety check. Use this when we want to push a behavior change behind a small slice (0.5–5%) and prefer human-in-loop inspection before broadening exposure.

Why a separate microactivation guide?
- Many of our existing rollout docs assume multiwave canaries or A/B tests with full experiment infra. Microactivations are faster, lower-friction, and more common for UI/UX prompts, heuristic toggles, or routing tweaks. They need a tighter ritual so we don’t accidentally ship noisy behavior.

Core roles (one-sentence responsibilities)
- Activation Steward: owns the decision to expand or retract; coordinates comms.
- Traffic Conductor: configures slices, throttles, and routing weights in the console.
- Observability Lead: wires up short-term dashboards and sanity queries.
- Safety Reviewer: spot-checks outputs and escalates quality issues.
- Cost Gatekeeper: watches cost delta and flags abnormal token spend.

Pre-flight checklist (quick pass, must be green)
- Hypothesis written (what user-visible change, expected metric delta)
- Minimal experiment config committed: slice id, start time, max exposure, fallback model/route
- Synthetic sim run: local sim with 2000 synthetic requests that mimic expected request mix
- Short dashboards: latency, 95th latency, error rate, user-facing quality sample stream
- Observability alerts created (soft thresholds for first 48h)
- Stakeholder ping list created and read by rostering stewards

Simulation script (fast local smoke)
1) Seed generation: pick representative prompt templates (n=12) from recent production logs or ticket examples.
2) Replay engine: run 2k requests through the staging route with the exact routing and model combo; capture top-k outputs.
3) Metric sweep: compute synthetic CTR-like proxies (matching product heuristics), mean token usage delta, and top-10 aberrant responses.
4) Failure injection: randomly replace 1% of requests with edge-case prompts (long tail) to test KV cache behavior.
5) Human sampling: Safety Reviewer reviews 100 sampled outputs, mark 'OK / Needs fix / Escalate'

Abort and rollback criteria (Tiered)
- Immediate abort (auto-retract): >1% requests return 5xx OR latency p95 > 5x baseline OR crash loop in serving.
- Fast abort (manual within 30m): safety reviewer escalation with reproducible quality regression on sampled outputs OR cost spike > 3x expected for initial slice.
- Slow revert (within 24h): metric drift beyond expected CI (CTR proxy or user completion rate) sustained for two observation windows.

Observation cadence and signal matrix
- 0–15m: real-time console + slack alert channel; watch error rate and p95 latency.
- 15–60m: hourly manual sampling from the sample stream; note any policy or harmful outputs.
- 1–24h: daily aggregated metrics, quality evaluation on canonical prompt set.
Signals to prioritize
- Safety flags: policy hits, toxicity classifier score spikes, hallucination heuristics
- Behavioral surprises: shift in most-likely token patterns, duplicate responses, truncated responses
- Latency & errors: p50/p95 and HTTP 5xx/4xx trends
- Cost: tokens per request and total tokens for slice

Lightweight experiment log (template entries)
- Activation id: micro-YYYYMMDD-<shortslug>
- Hypothesis summary: one line
- Start time / initial slice weight / fallback route
- Steward + Observability owner
- Sim results summary (counts: simulated requests, failure modes seen)
- First-hour notes and manual sample verdicts

Cross-team handoffs and comms
- Pre-activation: 1-line summary to #release-notices, attach sim summary and key dashboards
- Activation: ping oncall channel and a single-threaded Slack for steward coordination
- Post-mortem trigger: use lightweight post-mortem template if activation was aborted or required hotfix

Edge cases & operational notes
- If routing variant requires a different tokenization path (quantized model), run cost gatekeeper sim specifically for tokens-per-op; quantization can amplify hallucination in rare prompts.
- For hybrid inference (Hosted -> Dedicated fallback), ensure KV cache warm-up is simulated; cold-cache latency should be included in p95 baseline.
- Human-in-loop: prefer short batch windows (10–30 min) to keep reviewer fatigue manageable.

Open questions / TODO (notes to self)
- Automate the 2k-request sim via the rollout-sim repo and expose a 'micro-run' button in the console. (INF-4024)
- Create a lightweight checklist template in the Console UI (annex) so Traffic Conductors don't need a doc copy.
- Decide default synthetic sample size for different product surfaces (chat vs. reranker).

Appendix: quick SQL sanity queries (examples for Observability Lead)
- Recent 1h error rate: SELECT count(*) filter (where status >=500)/count(*) FROM requests WHERE route = '<route>' AND ts > now() - interval '1 hour';
- Sample stream: SELECT id, prompt, response, model FROM requests WHERE route = '<route>' AND ts > now() - interval '1 hour' ORDER BY random() LIMIT 100;

Notes to readers
This is a pragmatic, intentionally terse guide. If you are the first steward for a microactivation and you feel unsure, pause and pull in the Observability Lead — the simulation run usually surfaces the majority of weirdness.

Revision history
- 2025-01-15: initial draft (Sim script skeleton, roles, abort criteria)
- 2025-02-03: added SQL examples, expanded failure-injection notes
